title: Giving lawn parties and dances; Celestin remembered
summary: She gave lawn parties and dances, hired a blind pianist, and recalls Celestin playing in Slidell when she was ten.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Oh she knows who I was doing. I gave a lot of dances in life, and I gave a lot of lawn parters. And I made pretty good on them, you know. And I think, I wouldn't say if I was a little younger, I could really, now I could understand giving them, but I just wouldn't have anybody to go in with me, you know, to give them, you know. And you really had such a different opportunity. I don't know, the people was a lot different in some respects. And then you'd get a police, you could choose the police you want at the door, you could tell them which one you wanted to send. And you'd give people them days, big friends, you know, they had personal friends and everything, you know. And you could tell them what police to send you, to be at the door and all that kind of stuff. And they really made money, you know, selling tickets and all that. They made a lot of money. I gave a lot of game parties, you know, lawn parties. Everybody would come with game dresses, you know. And I had several times where I would all be playing for somebody else, where I'd have to get another band. I had a little fellow. The last dance I gave back, Taunty Street, a lawn party. The fellow would play it. I had Charlie, a blind Charlie, who was a piano player. And he could play. A blind fellow. You wouldn't think it would be blind. A lot of people used to kid and go on, because they wouldn't say Charlie was blind. They'd pass seeing him nailing a picket on his fence and all that. And you could tell the time, you know. He was great. They had really some great musicians a long time ago. And they really had a gift to that, you know. And it was, I don't know, it was plenty different. So it is, I don't say the youngsters ain't great today. They're really great. And, but them old time musicians, they're really good players. For instance, I could take Celestine and all that. Oh, they're really good players. And you know, often I wonder. I remember seeing Celestine about, I saw somebody, I saw Celestine about a year before he died. And do you know that Celestine was playing when I was a little child, about 10 years old. And he looked the same until he laid down and died from when I was 10 years old. I remember he used to come to Slidell and play for us with Manuel and them. He'd have two trumpets, you know. Manuel played a lot of times with him. And they had, what did I say, the superior.
